description: Hi, this is Arjoman looking for members who are interested in coding and app making with Android studio
summary:
Lost in Space is an AI-powered, interactive space exploration and educational app developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main idea is simple: instead of making students read boring fact sheets about abandoned spacecraft, it turns real NASA mission records into exciting mysteries that they can explore, investigate and solve. The app uses real missions to teach actual scientific concepts, example:
- Opportunity: How dust storms can affect solar power and end a mission.
- Surveyor 3: How astronauts revisited an old spacecraft and brought its camera back to Earth.
- InSight: How scientists study a planet's interior using marsquakes.
Instead of simply reading about these events, users make decisions, examine evidence and understand the science behind them and feel the engineering limits that ended the real missions
details:
Benefits - The game makes player feel the engineering limits that ended real missions through games and puzzles, example - Opportunity was solar powered- our game segment with the rover maze shows every move costs more battery- waste it and the rover stops. Our case file segment train claim evidence reasoning which helps student sto learn the science behind the missions, for example Evidence - Opportunity, solar panels, 2918 dust storms, Claim: the dust storm starved Opportunity of power - the student understands the reasoning that no sunlight, no charge so the rover could not survive the storm

Impacts - Students, science club members, space enthusiasts who want to learn in a fun engaging way. Other apps just inform, Lost in Space makes learners act on same facts. People remember what they had to work out. Lost in space wont let the retired missions fade from public memory

Tools- AI tools like chat gpt GPT 5, Gemini flash, Android studio, File explorer,

Languages - html, css, javascript, Kotlin

Our project is creative because it bridges the gap between what information exists and how that information is engaging to a 10 year old- We understood that NASA information exists but it is not engaging to a 10 year old. Existing space games exist like NASA's Explore Mars but no product connects real mission data to the questions that a 10 year old might ask. That is what our learning game app - Lost in Space does, it starts from the questions. Lost in Space turns NASA records into a learning loop.

Factors considered: Text to speech converter for folks with reading disabilities, easy UI and a chatbot Orbit which is scoped to curated mission records.
